question.leadin: The Battle of Inchon was a major offensive in this conflict, and this war ended with the establishment of the Demilitarized Zone at the 38th Parallel.
question.text: Name this conflict that ended with an armistice dividing a namesake peninsula.
question.answerHtml: Korean War [accept “Conflict” in place of “War;” or Hanguk Jeonjaeng; or Choguk haebang chonjaeng]
question.clue: Task Force Faith was disbanded after losing a battle on the east side of the Chosin Reservoir in this war, but U.S. marines to the south fought out of a Chinese encirclement.

swap.leadin: Give the following about medieval Asian warfare.
swap.text: In the 16th century, Yi Sun-sin perfected the design of the turtle ships used by the Joseon dynasty to defend this Asian peninsula from the invading Japanese navy. One modern country on this peninsula has capital Seoul.
swap.clue: The "Three Kingdoms" of this region included Baekje, Silla, and Goguryeo.

question.leadin: Answer the following about yellow ribbons in history.
question.text: Victims of the Sewol ferry disaster in this country are commemorated with yellow ribbons. The Miracle on the Han River refers to massive growth in this country's capital of Seoul.
question.answerHtml: South Korea [or the Republic of Korea; or ROK; prompt on Korea; reject “North Korea” or the “Democratic People’s Republic of Korea”]
question.clue: Nearly 300 high school students drowned on a ferry boat in this country in 2014.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about pyramids around the world.
swap.text: The pyramidal Ryugyong Hotel in this country remains unfinished despite its construction starting in 1987. A grand opening was planned in 2012 on the centenary of this country's "Eternal President" Kim Il-Sung, but it was eventually scrapped.
swap.answerHtml: North Korea [or Democratic People’s Republic of Korea; prompt on Korea]
swap.clue: A 2019 Summit between the U.S. and this nation hosted in Hanoi ended after a request to destroy the Yongbyon nuclear facility was refused by minister Ri Yong-ho.

question.leadin: This event transformed one country's economy from one of the poorest in the world to one of the largest in the region.
question.text: Name this event during which the emergence of Chaebol conglomerates helped spur the rapid modernization and economic growth of an Asian country.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the politics of South Korea.
swap.text: This president of South Korea favoured Korean reconciliation and unification, and met with Kim Jong-Un and US President Donald Trump in 2019. He also gained international praise for his handling of the Covid-19 pandemic.
swap.set: 2023 Politics & History with a side of Memes

question.text: With Goguryeo and Baekje, this kingdom that called itself Geunhwahyang was one of Korea's three kingdoms. A pseudo-military unit in this kingdom was the hwarang, its "flowering knights."
question.clue: This dynasty employed a cultured class of cosmetic-using soldiers called the "flowering knights," or "hwarang."

swap.text: Admiral Yi fought for this Korean dynasty, which ruled the peninsula after overthrowing the Goryeo.
swap.clue: As he died, a military leader of this kingdom instructed, "Beat my war drums. Do not announce my death."

question.text: This fourth emperor of the Joseon dynasty is credited with developing the phonetic Hangul writing system in the 1400s, though yangban elites resisted the change.
question.clue: It was said that an innovation from this monarch's reign could be learnt by wise men in a morning and by stupid men in ten days.

swap.leadin: Time to see how much you know about East Asian naval battles.
swap.text: In this last stand of the Korean navy, Admiral Yi Sun-Sin defeated a Japanese fleet of over 10 times his size with only 13 ships, destroying half the Japanese fleet. It is widely regarded as his greatest victory.
swap.clue: Joseon was invaded twice by Toyotomi Hideyoshi's forces in the Imjin War but were driven back at this 1597 naval engagement by Admiral Yi Sun-sin despite the Japanese outnumbering the Korean fleet at least 10 to 1.

question.leadin: For one of these groups to be officially recognized by the Court of the Lord Lyon, it must have a chief.
question.text: What are these kinship groups in which members often took the chief's surname and which often have a distinctive tartan pattern?
question.clue: What name is given to these family and extended groups identified by their differing tartans?

swap.leadin: Kings from this dynasty carried out purges of a faction of scholars known as the Sarim.
swap.text: Name this dynasty, an earlier king of which brought many scholars to his court in the Hall of Worthies. This dynasty fell into decline after its near-defeat in the Imjin War.
swap.clue: Members of the yangban (yong-bon) class were killed by followers of the "Eastern Learning" Donghak religion during this dynasty.

question.leadin: These campaigns are sometimes called the "Ceramic Wars" because potters were kidnapped and moved to Arita, where they developed one country's porcelain industry.
question.text: Name these campaigns during which soldiers reportedly cut off the noses of their victims as trophies because heads were too unwieldy to haul around.
question.answerHtml: Japanese invasions of Korea [accept Hideyoshi’s invasions of Korea; accept Imjin Wars]
question.clue: That one of these events eventually ended at the Battle of Noryang.

swap.text: The samin policy avoided the resettlement of this class of the Joseon gentry. Civil service exams known as gwageo selected this class, whose privileges were assailed in the failed Gapsin Coup.
swap.clue: This class which constituted the aristocracy of a kingdom which was the last to select its officialdom through the gwageo examination system.

question.text: In the initial phase of the war, North Korean forces pushed UN troops back to this feature, named for a very southern Korean city. The so-called "Bowling Alley" was one segment of this feature.

swap.leadin: The grievances that led to this event were later addressed by the Gabo Reform.
swap.text: Name this anti-yangban, anti-foreigner revolt that took place in 1894 and served as the catalyst for the Sino-Japanese war.
swap.clue: Mostly focused on the yangban class of the nobility, this movement drew from the earlier "Flower Boys" groups active in the Silla Kingdom.

question.leadin: Identify the following about Korean history FTPE.
question.text: This first native Korean state arose near the Yalu River in the first century CE and conquered the Chinese colony of Lolang.
question.clue: Under Yang, China attempted to conquer this kingdom, which opposed Baekje and Silla during the Korean Three Kingdoms Period. That invasion failed after the Battle of the Salsu River.

swap.text: The Unifed Silla employed this caste system to divide up the aristocracy using a measure of closeness to the throne. This system determined everything from the color of clothing worn to the maximum allowed size of the home.

question.leadin: He declared his namesake "line" in a 1952 speech in order to protect his country's interests in the Sea of Japan, including fishing rights around the Liaodong Rocks. FTPE.
question.text: Identify this man who died in exile in Hawaii, the first president of the Republic of South Korea.
question.clue: Jimmie Leach observed his crackdown of the April 3rd uprising on Jeju Island.

swap.leadin: This man's date with the bottom of the ocean in 1973 may have been averted through the quick action of ambassador Philip Habib, whom he later credited with helping to inspire his Nobel-winning Sunshine Policy.
swap.text: Identify this politician who failed thrice in his bid for the Presidency when not enduring hunger strikes, house arrests, or exile, prior to becoming the first Jeolla native to achieve the office.
swap.clue: Ambassador Philip Habib and Henry Kissinger supposedly intervened during an incident in which this man had weights tied to him and was almost drowned after he was kidnapped from a hotel in Tokyo.
